title: A Time-Multiplexed Q16.16 Fixed-Point Neural Network Accelerator for Resource-Efficient FPGA Inference
content: Deploying neural networks on edge devices requires a careful balance of speed, power, and area. FPGAs are well-suited for this task, but conventional floating-point arithmetic can incur significant hardware overhead. To address this challenge, this paper presents a multi-layer feedforward neural network accelerator designed for FPGA-based inference. The architecture employs a custom Q16.16 fixed-point format, offering a practical balance of numerical precision and hardware efficiency compared to floating-point units. A time-multiplexed data-path with a 64-bit accumulator, processes computations sequentially using a single MAC unit per neuron, aiming to reduce hardware consumption. This resource-conscious structure allows the network size to scale with modest increases in logic utilization. Deterministic saturation logic is implemented to help prevent overflow and contribute to stable operation under varying numerical conditions. The design was implemented entirely in VHDL and synthesized for an Artix UltraScale+ FPGA, achieving a maximum operating frequency of 139 MHz for a representative 4‑8‑8‑4 network, the accelerator requires only 520 LUTs, 1182 flip‑flops, and 4 DSP slices, corresponding to less than 1% of the available logic resources and requiring zero BRAM. One inference is completed in 233 clock cycles, yielding a throughput of approximately 597 K inferences per second. Verification using unit‑level testbenches and a 10,000‑iteration randomized stress test achieved 100% functional stability.
